tag.description: A grammatical tag: a bundle of an optional part of speech and any number of Feature=Value items, following Universal Dependencies. At least one of `upos`/`feats` must be present. A bundle, not an atom, because languages abbreviate at different granularities — French "nf." is one label for NOUN + Gender=Fem where Breton uses two. The tag carries no reader-facing text: the language record binds it to a label. Shared rather than defined per lexicon, because the same bundle is written by an entry (as a category), by a language (as the thing a label is bound to, and as the category a feature is inherent to) and later by a paradigm (as a cell address) — one shape, one home.

value.description: Part-of-speech name, e.g. "NOUN" — one of Universal Dependencies' 17 tags, or one a language minted.

scheme.description: Provenance. Absent means documented by Universal Dependencies; otherwise the BCP 47 tag of the language that minted it.

feature.description: Feature name, e.g. "Gender" or the layered "Number[psor]".

value.description: The value, e.g. "Fem". Several comma-separated values mean the item spans them all ("Gender=Fem,Masc").

scheme.description: Provenance of the feature/value pair as a whole — which is how a value minted on a UD feature is expressed ("Number=Sgv", scheme "br"). Per item, never per bundle: a bundle-level scheme could not describe a minted value sitting beside a UD part of speech.
